extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), commanders, and other Army personnel responsible for public affairs and news releases
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures for Army public affairs products and releases, including eligibility and limits for support to associations, restrictions on contractor hospitality, detailed rules for Nuclear/Biological/Chemical (NBC) accident/incident communications, notification chains, contingency releases, JIB operations, and publications/electronic media editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on annual support
rubrics_metrics.description: Army support to approved national military associations is limited to the annual conference or convention of each designated association, one conference or convention per calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements for military associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Military associations must be noncommercial in nature, national in scope, and must focus efforts on active duty, ARNG, and/or USAR activities; associations primarily oriented toward veterans or specific units, campaigns, gender, ethnic group, religion, or region do not meet eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the list of approved national military associations may be obtained from the OCPA. Approved associations generally will be added to the DOD-designated association list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized use of personnel and equipment for association support
rubrics_metrics.description: While on duty status, Army members are restricted to performing duties that relate directly to their designated military specialties; use of personnel and equipment must be at no additional cost to the Government, and logistical support must be incorporated into legitimate, scheduled training missions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited air transportation for conference attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: Military members traveling on official orders or space-available without orders may travel to and from conferences aboard military aircraft; civilian spouses not designated by the Services cannot use military air transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All such flights must be legitimate scheduled training missions and approved in advance by the OCPA to ensure propriety and cost effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited ground transportation for conference attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: Official conference attendees may travel to and from conferences and official conference functions by Government-owned or Government-contracted ground transportation, except travel to/from personal residences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VIP sedan transportation is restricted to general or flag grade officers and/or distinguished civilians of equivalent grade and their spouses. Spouse functions do not qualify for Army transportation. All plans involving Government-provided ground transportation must be approved in advance by the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited communications support
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited communications support may be provided for functions such as message distribution, communications systems management, automation services, and portable radio and cellular phone use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical assistance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical support may be provided only for support of emergency and lifesaving functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support limits and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative support (typing, filing, photocopying, distribution processing, telephone answering, accounting duties) may be provided only if directly related to official conference events and should be of reasonable duration, generally no more than 2 weeks prior to and 1 week after the officially announced dates of the conference or convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security support authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Security support may be provided if local civilian resources are not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement for such support must be documented by official requests from local civilian law enforcement agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting gratuities from contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting gratuities from private companies in connection with an association's activities is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as specified in 5 CFR 2635 and DOD 5500.7–R, Army civilian and active duty personnel are prohibited from attending social functions as guests of any contractor or potential contractor and from accepting hospitality from such contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for accepting invitations to contractor-sponsored association events
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitations to association banquets, luncheons, and similar events may be accepted only if the sponsoring organization demonstrates in advance that (1) the affair will have open seating, and (2) seating is neither selected nor influenced by contractor interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift acceptance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting gifts other than specialty advertising items of trivial intrinsic value for themselves or their families is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on contractor/industry-influenced guest lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitations to association functions should not be accepted unless the sponsor assures that no single contractor or industry-developed guest lists or seating plans reflect their special interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible Army participation with industry organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, Army participation will be limited to luncheons, dinners, meetings hosted by diverse-business organizations; public ceremonies mutual to industry and Army; industrial programs that support Government policy (e.g., industry-sponsored seminars, international exhibits); civic/community projects where industry relationship is separate from business purpose; and special events consistent with DOD 5500.7–R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include industry-sponsored seminars to explain Government policies, international exhibits promoting U.S. achievements, business-sponsored scouting activities for military families, and industry-subsidized awards for civic/community achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of unclassified material to industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclassified material and records for release outside of DA will be made available upon request to industry representatives or associations representing industry, consistent with AR 25–55 and chapter 3 of this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional community relations support to non-Government organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines do not prohibit Army support available to non-Government organizations; support can include designating DOD and Army coordinators, providing bands/troops/speakers, lending or leasing materiel, supporting major conventions of veterans organizations, and supporting other community relations activities governed by OCPA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public entitlement to unclassified accident information
rubrics_metrics.description: The public is entitled to all unclassified information concerning an accident when this regulation or other directives allow such release; furnishing such information in a positive manner is in the national interest and a command function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must know AR 50–5, AR 50–6, other AR 50-series regulations, AR 380–86, and requirements of this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuclear accident confirmation/denial policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of the Army policy is that, normally, the presence of nuclear weapons or nuclear components will not be confirmed or denied; however, in the event of a serious accident involving a nuclear weapon, official confirmation may be made when it will have public safety value or reduce/prevent widespread public alarm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The on-scene commander (OSC) may confirm or deny presence; the DDO, NMCC, may invoke exception before OSC based on available information and coordination with responsible Service chief. Notify OASD (PA) in advance if practicable or as soon as possible after initiating the exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological and chemical incident information release standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by valid security concerns, information on a serious incident involving biological or chemical weapons or agents will be provided to the public and news media in a timely and accurate manner consistent with requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releasing officials are specified in paragraph 5–3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release policy for nuclear reactors/facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible official will release information about the facility and nuclear materials only to the extent necessary to ensure public safety, prevent or reduce widespread public alarm, and ensure public understanding of the hazard and safety precautions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releasing information beyond this guidance must be approved in advance by the OCPA. Army policy is not to comment on facilities, nuclear materials, or matters involving agencies outside the Department of the Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearance for chemical munitions and NBC defense information
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to initial release of information on chemical munitions and NBC defense-related matters outside DOD, the information will be coordinated with the OCPA; new information may become a matter of national interest and must be cleared through OASD (PA) by the OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all Army agencies, contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for reusing cleared NBC material
rubrics_metrics.description: Material once cleared for public release may be used in subsequent releases only if (1) competent authority confirms information remains in conformance with current DOD policy, (2) original context of information has been preserved, and (3) no new material has been added.

rubrics_metrics.name: No commitment to release NBC defense information before clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: No commitment will be made to release chemical warfare and NBC defense information to any information medium until it has been properly cleared for release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance clearance for participation in NBC-related media appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation by Army agencies and individuals in television programs, on-camera interviews, or print media interviews primarily on chemical warfare or NBC defense will be cleared in advance with the OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy does not apply to FOIA requests processed under AR 25–55; OCPA will be notified as soon as possible through PA channels when FOIA releases occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA planning requirements for biological and chemical incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive PA planning (personnel, administrative, communications, logistical support) must take place well ahead of a scheduled exercise, operation, or anticipated contingency; plans must be prepared by ACOM commanders and commanders responsible for storage/handling/transportation of biological/chemical materials and reviewed/approved as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans prepared by overseas UC components must conform to their directives; CONUS components conform to this regulation; tenant activities coordinate with host installations; commanders must review plans at least annually and brief appropriate personnel every 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum PA plan measures for NBC incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: PA plans must include: (1) designation of a responsible official authorized to release information; (2) procedures governing release of information, taking pictures, and dealing with media; (3) checklist procedures for potential OSCs; (4) procedures to notify military/civilian personnel and dependents; (5) conditions for experienced PAO to assume responsibilities; (6) procedures for OSC to establish direct communication with OASD (PA) if public safety measures required; (7) procedures to establish communications with OCPA/AOC after delegation; (8) provisions for informing key local leaders and officials about hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model checklist for CONUS accidents involving radioactive materials is at appendix I; CEAT composition and JIB location guidance provided for nuclear incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and adaptation of contingency public announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Public announcements and conditions for OSC use during nuclear accidents require OCPA prior approval for adaptation to suit local contingencies; preplanned contingency releases (1–4) are used under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingency Release 1–No Danger: used when no public danger but official confirmation reduces alarm; Release 2–Possible Danger: used to notify local/state officials, neither confirms nor denies presence and not for general public; Release 3–Public Possibly in Danger: used for general public, neither confirms nor denies and must not go beyond sample; Release 4–Probably Danger: used when public probably in danger, confirms presence, information must not exceed sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial PA responsibility for nuclear weapon accidents
rubrics_metrics.description: In the United States, its territories, and possessions, OASD (PA) will retain initial PA responsibility for nuclear weapon accidents and significant incidents; overseas, unified commanders in coordination with OASD (PA) and Chief of U.S. Mission will have initial PA responsibility (with exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for confirming/denying presence of nuclear weapons at an accident
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of nuclear weapons or components may neither be confirmed nor denied except in specified circumstances: (1) in interest of public safety OSC may confirm presence; (2) to reduce/prevent widespread public alarm OSC may issue reassurance confirming or denying presence with appropriate assurances; (3) overseas, unified commanders with host government concurrence may confirm/deny in interest of public safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confirmation is made to protect public safety, notify public authorities timely and candidly and advise OASD (PA) as soon as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and operation of a Joint Information Bureau (JIB)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nuclear weapons accident or likely event occurs outside DOD/DOE facility boundaries, a JIB will be established near the scene as focal point for public release; OSC will establish JIB in coordination with DOE, FEMA, state, and local authorities; JIB will have dedicated administrative, communications, logistical support for all participating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSC will assume primary leadership/direction of JIB until transition; DOD PA activities must be coordinated with other agencies represented in JIB; senior FEMA official may establish/supervise JIB until OSC arrives; transfer of JIB responsibility to FEMA possible by mutual agreement, but DOD retains classification authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification-sensitive information handling during nuclear incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Most information on nuclear weapons and their storage is classified and very sensitive; OSC and responsible persons must follow contingency releases to preclude compromise of classified information; declassification requests referred to DOD for coordination with DOE as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of sensitive info include weapon design, whether a weapon contains tritium, tritium physical/chemical form, and specific weapon locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release authorities and procedures for biological/chemical accidents off-installation in CONUS
rubrics_metrics.description: If an accident occurs in CONUS outside a military installation, only the AOC, designated military person in charge, the OSC, the explosive ordnance disposal officer (through the on-scene PAO), or the technical escort officer may release information to properly identified news representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical escort officer is responsible for making news releases and notifications; if escort officer is a casualty, designated military person, OSC, or PAO will make releases; if mass casualties prevent this, nearest receiving military installation official will make releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-installation biological/chemical accident release procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For accidents on a CONUS installation or where agent may have escaped installation boundaries, the installation commander is responsible for making news releases through the PAO and for notifying proper authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public announcements tailored to local requirements should be incorporated into PA plans (appendix I contains sample announcements). If accidental release requires immediate warning/evacuation, request assistance from newspapers, local radio/TV, police and civil disaster relief agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas NBC incident release governance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an NBC accident/incident occurs overseas, release of information will be governed by applicable treaties, international agreements, host nation laws, Service-to-Service technical arrangements, and Army component/UC plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army components may constitute a JIB coordinating through the appropriate UC, Chief of U.S. Mission, and host nation authorities. Overseas commands must translate appendix I announcements into host country language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for NBC releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons making news releases on NBC accidents/incidents must notify by the fastest means available specified organizations depending on location (e.g., OASD (PA), OCPA, AMC PAO, FORSCOM PAO, nearest installation PAO, Movement Control Center), include release content and circumstances; OCONUS releases go through chain to NMCC; biological/chemical releases must notify OCPA fastest means and include content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCPA will notify other organizations outside chain of command on a need-to-know basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval for additional contingency releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Other releases or announcements (or modifications) may be included in nuclear accident/incident PA plans to suit local contingencies only if approval given in advance by the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct communications for NBC incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: PA communications channel should parallel the command communications channel, but to expedite PA actions in an NBC accident/incident, direct communication by the fastest means possible is authorized with the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary function of Army publications and electronic media
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary function of Army publications and electronic media is to support a commander's internal objectives: provide Armywide and local information; assist the commander in identifying and correcting command problems; act as tools for two-way communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See appendix J for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and news policy — free flow and no censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a free flow of news and information to all DA personnel without censorship or news management. The calculated withholding of news unfavorable to the DA is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and news policy — factual, objective, tasteful coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that news coverage is factual and objective. Select news and headlines using the dictates of good taste and avoid morbid, sensational, or alarming details that are unessential to factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and news policy — distinguish fact and opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between fact and opinion; when an opinion is expressed, identify the source. Accuracy and balance in coverage are paramount.
